metadata.description: azd environment name; names the resource group and seeds unique names.
Primary region. Defaults to the region chosen for the deployment itself, which the portal asks for.
Region for the Azure OpenAI account. Defaults to location.
Deploying user object id (AZURE_PRINCIPAL_ID); empty in CI.

Grant the person deploying the roles that need no key: Key Vault Secrets Officer and Cognitive Services OpenAI User (so sanity.sh can read secrets and call the model with its own token). azd passes AZURE_PRINCIPAL_ID and needs no flag. In the portal tick this: it uses deployer().objectId and assumes a user, not a service principal.
Chat model. Empty: the profile decides (demo and reference gpt-5.1, free-trial gpt-4.1-mini: a new subscription has no quota for gpt-5.4-nano).
Version of the chat model. Set it together with chatModelName.
Azure OpenAI API version the apps call. gpt-5.1 tool calling on the Responses API is unverified; see docs/azure-deployment.md.

Local (key) authentication on the AIServices account. auto: disabled when the apps use identity (free-trial, reference), enabled when they use the key (demo). Override with enabled to keep keys, for a tool that cannot use Entra ID.

auto: the profile decides (demo key, reference identity). key: apps read the account key from Key Vault. identity: Entra ID through the user-assigned identity (needs Azure P3 in the image) and local auth is disabled on the account.

false skips the Azure OpenAI account, its deployments and role, and the account-key secret. The apps then use externalLlmProvider. Needed where Azure OpenAI is unavailable or quota-zero (a free trial), or to keep a deployment at zero model spend. Not combinable with deployGateway, deployFoundryProject or the reference profile (both need the account).

Only when deployOpenAi is false. openai: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (externalLlmBaseUrl, key in Key Vault secret llm-api-key). replay: no model is called; chat prompts are answered from recordings only (the released images carry none, so chat reports "not recorded"; everything else works).
OpenAI-compatible base URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1. Required with externalLlmProvider openai.
Chat model name for externalLlmProvider openai. Needs a row in config/pricing/models.yaml or its cost is reported as unknown.
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER when deployOpenAi is false. replay (default) uses keyless hashing vectors, so a compatible endpoint without an embeddings route still works. Empty follows the chat provider.
API key for externalLlmProvider openai; stored as Key Vault secret llm-api-key. Empty for replay.
GHCR repository prefix the images are pulled from when imageSource resolves to ghcr.
Pinned image tag (release or sha-<7>). No default on purpose.
restricted (default): the frontend accepts only the deployer IP and ALLOWED_IPS. open: anyone, an open spend tap.
Deployer public IPv4 (set by preprovision). Allowed through the frontend ingress when restricted.
Extra CIDR ranges, comma separated, allowed through the frontend ingress when restricted.
AZ-2: create a Foundry project under the AIServices account, connect App Insights to it, grant the app identity Azure AI User.
Per-app identities: one user-assigned identity per app (modules/app-identities.bicep). Created but NOT attached to the apps; wiring is in apps.bicep and documented in docs/azure-deployment.md.
AZ-5: API Management in front of the model account; the apps call it instead. Provisioning takes minutes (v2 tiers) to 45 minutes (classic). See docs/azure-deployment.md.
UNVERIFIED which tiers support the Azure OpenAI token policies; see modules/gateway-apim.bicep.
APIM publisher email (service notices). Set a real one for a lasting gateway.
Tokens per minute for an agent without its own entry in gatewayAgentTokenLimits.
Per-agent tokens per minute by agent name, e.g. { orchestrator: 120000 }.
Login password of the seeded admin, support and seller accounts. Required: nothing generates it for you without azd.

Demo only. True seeds the documented demo passwords (admin123, support123, seller123) instead of the generated staff password. Honoured only while publicAccess is restricted; with open access it is ignored and the generated password is used.

Which implementation of the orchestrator, specialists and inventory MCP server runs. The outbox worker, db-init job, auth server, frontend and product MCP server are Python on both. dotnet is verified offline only.

Where the apps pull images from. auto: the profile decides (demo ghcr, reference acr). acr creates a registry; fill it with scripts/azure/acr-images.sh (az acr import from GHCR, or az acr build from source).
false creates everything except the container apps and the db-init job. Used for the first pass of an acr deployment, when the registry has to be filled before the apps can start.

metadata.description: Log Analytics workspace name.
Application Insights name.
Daily ingestion cap in GB, as a decimal string because the free-trial profile caps below one GB (the API minimum is 0.023). -1 disables the cap.
Vault name, 3-24 chars, globally unique.
Principal that reads secrets at runtime (the user-assigned identity).
Deploying user or pipeline; gets Secrets Officer. Empty to skip.
Reference profile: public network access off and the default firewall action Deny (trusted Azure services bypass). Reached through a private endpoint; secrets are still written through ARM.
Operator-supplied API key for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (free-trial path).
Write the postgres-admin-password secret. Nothing reads it (the apps use database-url, which carries the password); the free-trial profile turns it off so the password exists in one secret only.

Write a2a-identity-key, oauth-seed-key and auth-signing-key-encryption-key. The first is optional outside token mode (the key falls back to the agent secret) and the other two are read only with AUTH_MODE=oauth; the free-trial profile turns them off unless the auth server is deployed.
Write the llm-api-key secret. A plain flag, not !empty(llmApiKey): a secure value is not known when the template is evaluated offline.
Demo only: lets Azure-hosted services reach the server without a private endpoint.
Reference profile: public access off; the server is reached through a private endpoint.
Principal that calls the models with Entra ID (the user-assigned identity).
False while the apps authenticate with the account key (Azure P3 not merged); true once AZURE_OPENAI_AUTH=identity is the default.
AZ-2: lets Foundry projects be created under this account. Adds a system-assigned identity. Off leaves the account exactly as it was.
Reference profile: public network access off, reached through a private endpoint.
The person deploying (azd AZURE_PRINCIPAL_ID). Gets Cognitive Services OpenAI User so scripts/azure/sanity.sh can call the model with its own Entra token instead of an account key. Empty skips it.

responses or chat_completions (llmProvider openai); several compatible endpoints have no /responses route.

Wire the A2A user context: both (headers and signed token, default) or token (signed token only; needs a distinct A2A_IDENTITY_KEY, which preprovision generates).
Redis comes from Azure Managed Redis (a Key Vault secret) instead of the redis container app.
containerApps section of the profile.
Cost budget behaviour. enforce stops a run once it passes the per-run ceiling.
restricted: the frontend accepts only allowedIpRanges (default). open: anyone, which is an open spend tap.
True: the db-init job gets no SEED_STAFF_PASSWORD, so the seeder uses the documented demo passwords.
CIDR ranges allowed to reach the frontend when publicAccess is restricted.
Mount a2a-identity-key, oauth-seed-key and auth-signing-key-encryption-key. False (free-trial) when the auth server is off and the A2A key is the agent secret: those three are not in Key Vault then.

metadata.description: UNVERIFIED: tier support for the Azure OpenAI token policies is not confirmed offline. See the header.
APIM requires a publisher email; it receives service notices. Set a real one.
AIServices account the gateway fronts.
entra: the caller presents an Entra token (the apps identity). subscription: the caller presents an APIM subscription key as api-key, stored in Key Vault.
Client ids of the identities allowed to call (entra mode).
{ app, principalId } per app identity: the token oid vouches for the agent name (entra mode).
Key Vault that receives the subscription key as azure-openai-key (subscription mode).
Tokens per minute for an agent without its own entry in agentTokenLimits, and for names that are not listed.
Per-agent tokens per minute, by agent name.

variables.$fxv#0:
<policies>
  <inbound>
    <base />
    <!-- 1. Who is calling. Entra mode: validate the caller token (audience is the model scope),
         restricted to the app identities. Subscription mode: APIM already checked the key. -->
    {{CALLER_AUTH}}
    <!-- 2. Which agent. An app identity vouches for its name (trustedAgent). Without that the
         x-agent-name header is believed, and counted as untrusted. -->
    <set-variable name="trustedAgent" value="@{
      if (!context.Variables.ContainsKey("callerJwt")) { return ""; }
      var jwt = (Jwt)context.Variables["callerJwt"];
      var oid = jwt.Claims.GetValueOrDefault("oid", new string[] { "" })[0];
      foreach (var entry in "{{OID_MAP}}".Split(';')) {
        var pair = entry.Split('=');
        if (pair.Length == 2 && pair[0] == oid) { return pair[1]; }
      }
      return "";
    }" />
    <set-variable name="agent" value="@{
      var trusted = (string)context.Variables["trustedAgent"];
      if (trusted != "") { return trusted; }
      return context.Request.Headers.GetValueOrDefault("x-agent-name", "unknown");
    }" />
    <!-- 3. Per-agent token budget. A name that is not listed shares one bucket, so a made-up
         header cannot mint fresh counters. -->
    <choose>
      {{AGENT_LIMITS}}
      <otherwise>
        <azure-openai-token-limit counter-key="unlisted" tokens-per-minute="{{DEFAULT_TPM}}" estimate-prompt-tokens="true" remaining-tokens-header-name="x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens" />
      </otherwise>
    </choose>
    <!-- 4. Token metrics per agent to Application Insights (custom metrics, needs the
         diagnostics resource with metrics enabled). No request or response bodies are logged. -->
    <azure-openai-emit-token-metric namespace="ecommerce_agents">
      <dimension name="Agent" value="@((string)context.Variables["agent"])" />
      <dimension name="AgentTrusted" value="@(((string)context.Variables["trustedAgent"]) != "" ? "true" : "false")" />
      <dimension name="API ID" />
    </azure-openai-emit-token-metric>
    <!-- 5. Backend: the gateway own managed identity. The caller key never reaches the account. -->
    <set-header name="api-key" exists-action="delete" />
    <set-header name="Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key" exists-action="delete" />
    <authentication-managed-identity resource="https://cognitiveservices.azure.com" />
  </inbound>
  <backend>
    <forward-request timeout="230" buffer-response="false" />
  </backend>
  <outbound>
    <base />
  </outbound>
  <on-error>
    <base />
  </on-error>
</policies>

      ')]
